subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the macula

steps.tx: **Dry age related macular degeneration** affects elderly smokers with family risk and pale fundi. **Drusen** appear as discrete deposits or soft confluent patches with pigment clumping, bending lines on the Amsler grid while sparing the periphery. Large soft drusen with pigment change mark intermediate disease with higher conversion risk. **AREDS2** antioxidants with zinc slow intermediate progression in selected patients while smoking cessation and Mediterranean patterns protect. Geographic atrophy spreads as sharply demarcated chorioretinal loss and advances centrally despite supplements, needing low vision aids.
steps.say: Dry macular degeneration is the disease that seeds yellow deposits under the retina in older adults, especially smokers. The deposits clump pigment and are the reason straight lines bend on the Amsler grid while side vision stays normal. Large soft deposits with pigment change mark intermediate disease with higher risk of turning wet. Antioxidant supplements slow intermediate disease in selected patients and quitting smoking protects both eyes. Central bald patches of atrophy spread slowly and they need low vision aids.

steps.tx: This fundus photo shows **soft drusen** as yellow deposits with dark **pigment clumping** and a pale patch of geographic atrophy near the disc. Drusen with pigment change mark intermediate dry degeneration with rising risk of conversion to wet disease. Geographic atrophy shows sharply defined loss where retina and pigment have vanished. The image teaches the exam triad of drusen, pigment and atrophy on one macula. Recognising this triad guides AREDS2 use, Amsler advice and low vision support.
steps.say: This fundus photo is a view of yellow soft deposits with dark pigment clumps and a pale bald patch near the disc. The deposits with pigment change mark intermediate dry degeneration with rising risk of wet conversion. The pale patch shows geographic atrophy where retinal layers have disappeared. The triad teaches examiners to link drusen with pigment and atrophy in one eye. Spotting this pattern guides supplements, grid checks and low vision support.

steps.tx: **Wet neovascular degeneration** bleeds or leaks beneath the macula with subretinal blood, fluid and pigment epithelial detachment, crashing central vision. OCT with fluorescein or OCT angiography confirms choroidal new vessels. **Anti VEGF** injections dry and stabilise most eyes with loading then treat and extend patterns, with endophthalmitis and systemic cautions counselled. Photodynamic therapy suits polypoidal variants. Delay scars into a permanent disciform scar. Fellow eye Amsler self monitoring catches conversion early while smoking control protects.
steps.say: Wet degeneration grows new vessels under the macula that bleed and leak fluid. Central vision crashes within days and the scan shows blood with fluid lifting the pigment layer. Anti vessel injections dry the leak and they stabilise most eyes when treatment starts early. Delay lets the bleed scar into a permanent disciform patch that never recovers. The fellow eye needs grid self checks because early conversion saves reading vision.

vis.alt: Optical coherence tomography scan of the macula revealing choroidal neovascularization, subretinal fluid, and pigment epithelial detachment, characteristic of wet age-related macular degeneration.
vis.caption: OCT of wet AMD showing choroidal neovascularization with subretinal fluid. Image: Huang, XF., Huang, ZQ., Lin, D. et al., CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Interface disorders wrinkle or split the centre. **Macular hole** forms a full thickness foveal defect with a positive Watzke Allen slit sign from vitreous traction in elderly eyes. It needs vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peel and face down gas posturing for closure while lamellar holes mostly observe. **Epiretinal membrane** wrinkles the surface with a cellophane reflex and metamorphopsia and peels when reading fails. Vitreomacular traction with oedema releases by vitrectomy in debated ocriplasmin roles. Pseudoholes mimic with intact outer layers on OCT.
steps.say: A full thickness hole breaks the fovea and it snaps the narrow slit beam on testing. Vitreous traction pulls the centre open in older eyes, so vitrectomy with membrane peeling and face down positioning closes the defect. A surface membrane wrinkles the macula like cellophane and it bends straight lines, so peeling restores reading when glasses fail. Traction with swelling also benefits from release, while a pseudohole keeps outer layers intact on the scan.

steps.tx: Other maculopathies favour young patients or long eyes. **Central serous chorioretinopathy** strikes stressed men and steroid users with a smokestack leak and settles with trigger removal. **Myopic maculopathy** complicates long eyes with lacquer cracks, Fuchs spot and choroidal new vessels needing anti VEGF treatment with surveillance. Stargardt disease shows a beaten bronze macula with flecks in ABCA4 inheritance and counsels against vitamin A excess with sun protection while gene trials run. Best vitelliform disease shows an egg yolk lesion with EOG change and observes. Solar burns scar photoreceptors with history.
steps.say: Central serous disease blurs one eye in a young stressed adult, often after steroid use, and it usually settles once the trigger stops. Highly myopic eyes develop cracks and dark spots with new vessels that need anti vessel treatment and lifelong checks. Stargardt disease flecks a teenager macula with a beaten bronze look and it counsels against excess vitamin A with sun protection. Best disease holds an egg yolk lesion with an abnormal electrical response and it mostly observes, while sungazing burns the centre permanently.
